task_1.title: Fix source installs that invoke build-requirement CLI tools
task_1.description: Poetry 1.7.1 fixes a source-installation bug where building an sdist dependency could fail if the package's build process invoked a command-line tool supplied by its declared build requirements. The installer now preserves an isolated build environment that makes those build-time tools discoverable during dependency preparation.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that installing a dependency from an sdist succeeds when the package's build step invokes CLI tools provided by its declared build requirements, rather than failing because those tools are unavailable during the isolated source build.

expectation.grounded: When installing or preparing a dependency from source, Poetry must run the build inside an isolated build environment where console scripts exposed by packages in the project's build-system requirements are available to the backend during dependency preparation.
expectation.conceptual: Source builds should be able to execute command-line tools that come from their declared build dependencies. If a package's build scripts rely on those tools, installation should complete normally as long as the build requirements are correctly declared.

constraints.grounded: Keep source builds isolated, continue installing declared build-system requirements for the build environment, and limit the behavioral change to making build-requirement CLI entry points discoverable during source preparation without changing unrelated installation flows.
constraints.conceptual: Maintain the existing isolated-build model. The fix should only make valid build-time tools available during source builds and should not alter unrelated dependency resolution or standard installation behavior.

behavior: When Poetry builds a dependency from an sdist, CLI entry points installed from the dependency's declared build requirements are available during backend execution.
A source dependency build no longer fails solely because its setup or build step invokes a build-requirement command that was installed into the isolated build environment.
Dependencies built from source continue to use an isolated environment with declared build requirements installed before the package build runs.
acceptance_criteria: When installing a dependency available as an sdist whose build step invokes a CLI provided by a declared build requirement, the installation should succeed without manual PATH adjustments.
When a source build requires a command-line tool from its build dependencies, Poetry should make that command available during build execution in the isolated environment.
When building source dependencies that do not invoke build-requirement CLI tools, Poetry should preserve the existing isolated build behavior.

task_3.title: Fix `poetry init` dependency addition regression
task_3.description: Poetry 1.7.1 fixes a regression where `poetry init` could fail while adding dependencies because dependency lookup needed package index access before a `Poetry` project object was available. The initialization flow should continue to support dependency discovery during project creation and still honor the configured installer worker limit.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `poetry init` can add dependencies during project initialization without failing when dependency lookup occurs before a `Poetry` object has been created.

expectation.grounded: During `poetry init`, dependency lookup must be able to initialize the PyPI repository pool even when no `Poetry` object exists yet, and that lookup must continue to honor the configured `installer_max_workers` setting.
expectation.conceptual: `poetry init` should let users search for and add dependencies as part of creating a project, without crashing because initialization state is incomplete, while preserving the user's configured lookup concurrency behavior.

constraints.grounded: Do not require a pre-created `Poetry` object or existing project state as a prerequisite for dependency lookup inside `poetry init`. Do not regress the use of the configured installer worker count when creating the PyPI-backed lookup pool.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should only remove the initialization-time failure. Dependency addition during project setup should keep working the same way for users aside from no longer failing prematurely, and existing concurrency-related configuration should still apply.

behavior: When `poetry init` needs package index access to add dependencies, it should be able to construct its PyPI lookup state before a project-level `Poetry` object exists.
Adding dependencies during `poetry init` should no longer abort due to configuration access that depends on an already-initialized project object.
The PyPI lookup used by `poetry init` should continue to use the configured `installer_max_workers` value when determining lookup concurrency.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs `poetry init` and chooses or specifies dependencies that require package lookup, the initialization flow should proceed instead of failing before the project is created.
When dependency lookup is triggered during `poetry init` before any `Poetry` object is available, the command should still initialize its package source access successfully.
When the user has a non-default `installer_max_workers` configuration, dependency lookup during `poetry init` should respect that configured worker limit.

task_2.title: Restore symlinked sdist installs on affected Python releases
task_2.description: Poetry 1.7.1 fixes tar-based source distribution installation when archives contain symlinks and the host Python runtime has a broken `tarfile` data filter. The update bypasses that faulty standard-library path only on affected interpreter patch releases so installs succeed again without changing extraction behavior more broadly.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that installing a source distribution that contains symlinks succeeds on affected Python runtimes. Ensure that the installer bypasses the broken tarfile filtering path only where necessary and preserves existing extraction behavior elsewhere.

expectation.grounded: When Poetry extracts an sdist tar archive during installation, it should treat CPython 3.8.17, 3.9.17, 3.10.12, and 3.11.4 as affected runtimes and avoid the `tarfile` `"data"` extraction filter on those versions so symlink-containing sdists can be installed. On other Python versions that expose a working `tarfile.data_filter`, extraction should continue to use filtered tar extraction.
expectation.conceptual: Installing source distributions that contain symlinks should work on Python releases whose standard tar extraction filter is broken. The workaround should be narrowly scoped so unaffected environments continue to receive the normal safer extraction behavior.

constraints.grounded: Do not change zip archive extraction behavior. Do not disable filtered tar extraction on Python versions that support a working `tarfile.data_filter`. Preserve the existing unfiltered fallback on Python versions where `tarfile.data_filter` is unavailable.
constraints.conceptual: Only the known-bad tar extraction environments should switch to the compatibility path. Other archive types and unaffected Python environments should behave the same as before.

behavior: Tar-based sdist extraction skips the `tarfile` `"data"` filter on CPython 3.8.17, 3.9.17, 3.10.12, and 3.11.4.
On Python versions with a working `tarfile.data_filter`, tar-based sdist extraction continues to use filtered extraction.
On Python versions without `tarfile.data_filter`, tar-based extraction continues to use the existing unfiltered fallback.
sdists that include symlinks are no longer blocked from installation solely because the host runtime exposes the broken tar filtering implementation.
acceptance_criteria: When Poetry installs an sdist tar archive containing symlinks on CPython 3.8.17, 3.9.17, 3.10.12, or 3.11.4, the package should install successfully instead of failing during archive extraction.
When Poetry installs an sdist tar archive on a Python version that provides a working `tarfile.data_filter`, it should continue to follow filtered tar extraction behavior.
When Poetry installs an sdist tar archive on a Python version that does not provide `tarfile.data_filter`, the installation outcome should remain unchanged from the existing unfiltered fallback.
When Poetry installs a package from a zip archive, extraction behavior should be unchanged by this fix.

task_4.title: Handle installs in environments without virtualenv metadata
task_4.description: Poetry 1.7.1 fixes a failure during `poetry install` when virtualenv creation is disabled and the active Python environment does not provide `pyvenv.cfg`. Environment inspection should treat missing virtualenv metadata as a valid non-system-site-packages state instead of aborting the install.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `poetry install` succeeds when `virtualenvs.create` is set to `false` and Poetry uses an existing Python environment that does not include virtualenv metadata such as `pyvenv.cfg`.

expectation.grounded: When `virtualenvs.create` is `false`, environment handling that evaluates `VirtualEnv.includes_system_site_packages` must tolerate a missing `pyvenv.cfg`. In that case, the environment should be treated as not including system site packages, and `poetry install` should continue without failing during environment inspection.
expectation.conceptual: When Poetry is configured to install into the current interpreter instead of creating a new virtual environment, it should accept environments that do not expose virtualenv configuration files. Missing virtualenv metadata should be treated as a normal case, not an installation error.

constraints.grounded: Behavior for environments that do have `pyvenv.cfg` must remain consistent: `include-system-site-packages = true` should still be recognized as enabled, and all other cases should remain disabled. The fix should only make missing `pyvenv.cfg` non-fatal.
constraints.conceptual: Do not change how valid virtual environments are interpreted. Only prevent missing metadata from breaking installation, while preserving the existing meaning of explicit system-site-packages configuration.

behavior: `poetry install` no longer fails solely because the active environment lacks `pyvenv.cfg` when `virtualenvs.create` is disabled.
Environment inspection treats an absent `pyvenv.cfg` as `includes_system_site_packages = false` instead of causing a file access failure.
If `pyvenv.cfg` is present and explicitly enables system site packages, Poetry continues to recognize that environment as including system site packages.
acceptance_criteria: When a project runs `poetry install` with `virtualenvs.create` set to `false` in a Python environment without `pyvenv.cfg`, the install should proceed without failing during environment detection.
When Poetry inspects an environment that has no `pyvenv.cfg`, it should treat system site packages as disabled rather than raising an error.
When Poetry inspects an environment whose `pyvenv.cfg` explicitly enables system site packages, it should continue to report that state correctly.
